title: Data & Binary: Foundations
welcome_lead: Computers only know 0 and 1 — but that is enough for everything.
meta_desc: KS3 binary: bits, bytes, why computers use base 2.
final_note: Once you can read binary, the computer stops looking like magic.

concepts.def: A number system using only 0 and 1.
The everyday number system using 0 to 9.
How many different digits a system uses.

walkthroughs.body_html: Computers use switches that are either on or off. Two states map perfectly to 1 and 0. Everything — text, pictures, sound — is stored as long strings of these bits.
A bit is one 0 or 1. Eight bits make a byte. A byte can store 256 different values, enough for one English character.
1024 bytes is a kilobyte, 1024 KB is a megabyte, and 1024 MB is a gigabyte. Your phone has billions of bytes of storage.
